title: Interpreting an urban indicator coefficient
scenario_markdown: A generic retail example uses $\hat y=20+3x+8D$, where y is weekly revenue in thousands of dollars, x is advertising spending in thousands of dollars, and D=1 for urban stores and 0 for rural stores. The model has no interaction term. Predict an urban store's revenue when x=10 and interpret the indicator. Dummy-variable assessment coverage is not yet confirmed for this course.
assumptions: Rural stores (D=0) form the reference category; urban stores have D=1.
The model is additive with a common advertising slope and no interaction.
Indicator-variable teaching is generic pending course confirmation; association alone is not causal.

stages.prompt_markdown: What is predicted weekly revenue for x=10 and D=1, in thousands of dollars? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: An urban store has D=1, so include the indicator term.
Multiply advertising by 3 and the indicator by 8; do not swap them.

stages.prompt_markdown: At the same advertising spending, what is the predicted urban-minus-rural difference, in thousands of dollars? Select the value rounded to four decimal places.

options.hint_markdown: The advertising slope describes changes in x, not the category difference.
The urban intercept includes the baseline; the difference between intercepts is the dummy coefficient.

stages.explanation_markdown: The rural intercept is 20 and urban intercept is 28. Their difference is 8, independent of x in this additive model.

stages.prompt_markdown: Which interpretation is supported by this additive model?

options.text_markdown: Holding advertising fixed, urban stores have predicted weekly revenue 8 thousand dollars higher, with the same advertising slope.
Urban advertising has slope 11 instead of 3.
options.hint_markdown: Different slopes require an interaction term such as x times D.

options.text_markdown: Moving any rural store to an urban location is guaranteed to add 8 thousand dollars of revenue.
options.hint_markdown: A regression association does not establish an intervention effect.

stages.explanation_markdown: The indicator shifts the intercept, not the advertising slope. Both category lines have slope 3. The fitted contrast controls for included advertising, but unmeasured differences may remain.
